reasons: The test uses LR04 benthic d18O as a global proxy for ice volume/deep-water temperature and EPICA Dome C deuterium-derived temperature as a Southern high-latitude temperature record, which are reasonable stand-ins for global glaciation and regional temperature (read_edc, read_lr04). Simultaneity is operationalized as a high lagged correlation (>=0.6) between Antarctic temperature and −d18O over 0–800 ka with ±6 kyr allowance (analysis: max Pearson correlation over lags −6..+6), which captures broad in-step behavior but only for one hemisphere and a global stack rather than multiple regional temperatures. The “long-lasting glacial states” criterion uses a fixed threshold d18O ≥ 4.0‰ on a 0–2600 ka grid with ≥10 kyr duration and ≥5 occurrences, which is an arbitrary operationalization and extends beyond the late Pleistocene focus implied by “the Glacial period” (mainly the last ice age), risking mismatch with the historical claim. Linear interpolation to 1-kyr spacing and the ±6 kyr lag window are broadly compatible with the age-model uncertainties of these datasets, though correlation across the full 0–800 ka window may reflect shared orbital pacing rather than strict event-by-event simultaneity. The pre-registered rule may fail a case where the last glacial was globally synchronous if criterion A fails for earlier intervals, so it does not cleanly isolate the simultaneity core of the claim.
what_would_change_it: Add independent high-latitude Northern Hemisphere temperature (e.g., Greenland or well-dated speleothem composites) and test multi-region synchrony directly (e.g., phase alignment or event matching) rather than Antarctic-only correlation to a global stack. Refocus criterion A on the last glacial cycle (e.g., 0–150 ka) or use a glacial–interglacial state definition tied to LR04’s established marine isotope stages instead of a fixed 4.0‰ threshold over 0–2600 ka. Expand/validate age-model alignment (e.g., larger lag window or explicit age-uncertainty propagation) and test synchrony around the LGM window specifically.
